title: Show your work
lede: Primary sources first. SEC filings link to the original text on EDGAR (Adolph Coors Company, later Molson Coors, CIK 24545). Zima was a brand inside a brewer, so the filings give percentages and context, not a product-level income statement.

notes.label: Derived
notes.text: 1995 volume of 663,000 barrels = 1.3M × (1 − 0.49), from the 49% decline in the 10-K[^3]. Zima’s 6.4% share of Coors’s 1994 volume = 1.3M ÷ 20.4M[^2]. “All other Coors brands” = company total minus Zima. Coors Light at 27 times Zima in 2000 = 16.6M ÷ 0.61M[^13]. The $55.1M rise in total advertising = $327.6M − $272.5M[^3]. Because the 1994 base is itself a rounded figure, every figure derived from it is approximate.

notes.label: The 1994 volume
notes.text: Coors did not publish it. The brand manager said in 1995 that Zima “almost hit 1.3 million barrels”[^12], and Slate gives 1.3 million[^13]. We use 1.3 million as a rounded figure. A figure of 1.2 million attributed to Brandweek is **unverified**: we could not locate the original.

notes.label: Estimates
notes.text: The $50 million 1994 advertising budget is a Denver Post **estimate** reported by Westword[^12]. The $38 million and $38.3 million figures are reported by Slate and by the Arizona Republic via Westword; Coors did not confirm either[^12][^13]. The 70% trial rate is Coors’s own **estimate** as reported by Slate[^13]. The $3.5 million development cost is described by Westword as “reported”[^12]. Japanese sales of over a million cases are as reported by The Daily Beast, without a named source[^29].

notes.label: Unverified or conflicting
notes.text: The year of the Japanese launch is given as 1996 by MillerCoors[^26] and 1997 by Hakutsuru[^31]. A $180 million launch budget in one retrospective[^34] is **unverified** and not used. A widely repeated claim that the 2017 run was 39,000 barrels, and that 2018 inventory was 40% larger, could not be traced to a source we could open; MillerCoors’s own blog says 20% more[^26]. Airing years of the commercials come from the uploaders. Zima Gold’s “about three months” is Slate’s characterisation[^13]; Westword dates the national launch to May 1 and the withdrawal to the month before its September 6, 1995 article[^12].

notes.label: Unknown
notes.text: Zima’s revenue, profit and advertising spend in any year; its volume in 1992–93, 1997–99 and 2001–08; the size of the 2017 and 2018 runs; current Japanese volumes; the result of the Retrobrands trademark application.

notes.label: Sources seen only in quotation
notes.text: The Washington Post’s March 1993 report is quoted from a 2017 column[^25]; Letterman’s jokes and Coors’s 1995 second-quarter release are quoted from Westword[^12]. We could not open New York Times, Los Angeles Times or Advertising Age articles from 1993–95, so none is cited.

notes.label: General knowledge
notes.text: A U.S. beer barrel is 31 gallons. Labor Day is the first Monday of September.

notes.label: Images
notes.text: Screenshots are Internet Archive captures of zima.com[^33]. Two photographs are from Wikimedia Commons under CC BY 3.0 and CC0, credited in the gallery. Drawings are original.
